title: Are 576 and 327 perfect squares, and what is the root?
description: The video decides which of five hundred seventy six and three hundred twenty seven is a perfect square, and finds its square root by trial. Keeko doubts the root after taking half of the number.
teaching_notes: One idea: use the last digit to rule a number out, then use known squares to trap the root between two tens and test the numbers in between. Watch for students who halve the number to get the square root.

source: Decide whether 576 and 327 are perfect squares, and find the square root of the one that is.
video_script.why: The child learns to rule out a non square by its last digit, and to find a square root by trapping it between two tens and testing the numbers between.
video_script.substitution: Rule out numbers by the last digit, square the nearby tens, and test the numbers in between.
video_script.anchor: the numbers five hundred seventy six and three hundred twenty seven, each with a yes or no box
video_script.wrong_move: Keeko halves 576 to get 288 and calls that the square root. But 288 × 288 = 82944, far more than 576; the root of 576 is 24, because 24 × 24 = 576.
video_script.payoff_line: Only five hundred seventy six is a perfect square, and its square root is twenty four

final_answer.value: Only 576 is a perfect square, and √576 = 24
final_answer.spoken: only five hundred seventy six is a perfect square, and its square root is twenty four

hold_back: Only 576 is a perfect square, and √576 = 24
never_show: the square root of 441 of the exercise video
maths_rules: 327 ends in 7, and no square ends in 7, so 327 is not a perfect square
20² = 400 and 30² = 900, so the root of 576 is between 20 and 30
ground: the last digits of 1² to 9² are 1, 4, 9, 6, 5, 6, 9, 4, 1
video_script.design: One idea: rule out by the last digit, then trap the root and test. Wrong idea: the root is half the number. The two numbers stay in the anchor band and the tests fill in on the working board.

narration: <bookmark mark='book'/>This question is from your book.
<bookmark mark='term'/>A perfect square means the square of a natural number. Its square root means the number that was squared.
<bookmark mark='nums'/>Look at five hundred seventy six and three hundred twenty seven.
<bookmark mark='ask'/>Is each of them a perfect square, and what is the square root of the one that is?

narration: <bookmark mark='seven'/>Step one, three hundred twenty seven ends in seven.
<bookmark mark='none'/>No square ends in seven, so three hundred twenty seven is not a perfect square.

beats.on_screen: 20² = 400 and 30² = 900; 576 lies between them; the root is between 20 and 30

marks.thirty: 30² = 900 is written and 576 is placed between them

narration: <bookmark mark='twenty'/>Step two, twenty squared is four hundred.
<bookmark mark='thirty'/>Thirty squared is nine hundred. Five hundred seventy six lies between them, so its root is between twenty and thirty.
<bookmark mark='first'/>Step three, test the numbers one by one. Twenty one squared is four hundred forty one, and twenty two squared is four hundred eighty four.
<bookmark mark='second'/>Twenty three squared is five hundred twenty nine.
<bookmark mark='hit'/>Twenty four squared is five hundred seventy six, which is the number we want.

marks.four: 24 × 4 = 96 is written and the two parts are added to 576

narration: <bookmark mark='twenty'/>Step four, put the answer back in the question. Twenty four times twenty is four hundred eighty.
<bookmark mark='four'/>Twenty four times four is ninety six, and the two parts add up to five hundred seventy six.

beats.on_screen: Answer: Only 576 is a perfect square, and √576 = 24
narration: <bookmark mark='ans'/>Only five hundred seventy six is a perfect square, and its square root is twenty four.
<bookmark mark='hand'/>Keeko has raised a hand. Let us check the doubt and solve it.

beats.on_screen: Keeko's bubble: half of 576 is 288, so the square root is 288; 288 × 288 = 82944 appears beside 576

marks.doubt: Keeko's bubble shows half of 576 is 288
marks.big: 288 × 288 = 82944 appears beside 576 and is far bigger

narration: <bookmark mark='doubt'/>Keeko thinks the square root is two hundred eighty eight. That is half of five hundred seventy six.
<bookmark mark='big'/>But two hundred eighty eight times itself is over eighty thousand, far more than five hundred seventy six.
<bookmark mark='fix'/>The root is much smaller than half, and here it is twenty four.
